The CYP3A4 active site is a large, primarily hydrophobic chamber with considerable conformational flexibility. Unlike CYP2D6 (which requires a basic nitrogen) or CYP2C9 (which prefers acidic substrates), CYP3A4 has no strong electrostatic selectivity — it accommodates neutral, basic, and acidic compounds. High lipophilicity (logP > 2-3) facilitates partitioning into the hydrophobic cavity. Multiple aromatic rings or extended hydrophobic surfaces.
